business_problem: Claims Connection Group needed to replace slow, fragmented and manual property-insurance claims handling so it could respond faster during disaster-driven spikes, interpret policy language more consistently, and reduce compliance and operational risk across the claims value chain.
solution_summary: Claims Connection Group rebuilt its claims operation as an AI-driven digital platform using IBM's watsonx portfolio, IBM Business Automation Workflow, IBM Robotic Process Automation and IBM watsonx Orchestrate. Watsonx is used to interpret complex insurance language and guide decision-making, while Business Automation Workflow coordinates collaboration across policyholders, agents, carriers and vendors. Robotic Process Automation removes repetitive clerical work, and watsonx Orchestrate binds the tools and processes together behind one cohesive interface for the end-to-end claims experience. The result is not a single point tool but a connected claims stack that can handle high-volume surge events more predictably: policyholders get clearer coverage information, agents and brokers move faster, carriers see fewer compliance delays, and vendors receive more structured task assignments during events such as hailstorms and heavy rains.

data_flow: Claim information and policy language enter the watsonx-driven platform, Business Automation Workflow routes work among adjusters and partners, Robotic Process Automation completes repetitive actions, and watsonx Orchestrate presents the combined process as a single operating interface.
business_outcome: CCG accelerated claims resolution, reduced manual effort and operating cost, improved transparency during catastrophe events, and created a more resilient and compliant claims experience for partners and end customers.

The workflow is designed to handle storm-driven spikes in claim volume.
The implementation digitized a traditionally manual claims process end to end.
